Either running from outside was the difference, or the earlier failures were the live session holding the directory - unresolved, and worth knowing rather than carrying forward as certain. ORDERING, WHICH THE DEVELOPER GOT RIGHT AND THE PLANNER HAD BACKWARDS: push and merge the session record FIRST, then exit, then move. RECOMMENDED, and it is a sequencing question rather than a design one: retention should TOMBSTONE rather than delete - id, title, sessions and a pointer - or refuse to evict a task whose id appears anywhere in the tracked tree, or at minimum report the eviction as a WARNING the writer has to acknowledge rather than one line among several.

--- AMENDED AT LOOP 16 CLOSE (session 76, 2026-09-21) ---
THE RANKING HALF, MEASURED IN LOOP 16 (amendments 10–11 at 084cf18, e0c1dd2): against ten genuine same-topic competitors each carrying all three derived terms, entry 299 ranks 4th of 11 (developer, comparable length) and 3rd (QA); on the live store it ranks 1st of 5 only because five entries carry all three terms — a thin field, not discrimination. Cause: bm25's length preference among documents that all match. Developer's key-column weighting table: ×2 → 5th, ×3 → 3rd, ×5 → 2nd, ×10 → 1st by 0.56 — a weight chosen to pass a test is tuning to the test, so none was chosen (R26: A1 asserts precision, reports the rank). Mitigation observed: the ten competitors gave the same advice as 299. This is the loop that owns ranking's evidence; not built in Loop 16.
- Gap G-027: expected_revision serialises writes within one lineage, not across branches. Two seats can read the same base revision, derive the same successor, and both be accepted - the collision is invisible at the data layer and surfaces only as a git conflict at merge time, a different and much later layer. The revision counter does less work than its name implies.
- Gap G-028: The stated reason for PR #33 - that the 115 findings were 'almost all files under .gitnexus/' - is false, and it is the sentence that made the trade-off look free. Measured: .gitnexus/ accounts for 19 of the 115 findings (16.5%) across 5 files. The other 96 come from real untracked documents: docs/superpowers/plans and specs, docs/dream-design.md, docs/mailbox-transport-retirement-spec.md, .agents/SYSTEM/ENTITIES.md and .agents/TASKS/research-wiki-audit.md. The fix is still right - untracked files do not ship, and re-deriving .gitignore by hand is the defect the check exists to find - but it suppresses 43 files naming a retired thing, not 5.
- Gap G-029: The regression test added by PR #33 can pass without testing anything. It runs `git init && git add && git commit` inside try/catch with stdio ignored, and on any failure does a bare `return` before reaching its assertion - so a machine without git, or with a git that fails for any reason, reports the test green. It is the rule 11 family - an instrument that cannot distinguish 'nothing there' from 'I did not look' - inside the regression test for the check about exactly that defect class.
- Gap G-030: Core cannot be installed and started by a stranger, and the reason is one finding with two halves - neither of them in the code. (a) THE DOCUMENTED ROUTE GOES THROUGH MEMORY: .claude/commands/start.md names ob_start six times and ob_set_session once and gives no CLI path, so anyone following the documented /start reaches server.ts and dies at module load on better-sqlite3 - even though every piece /start actually needs runs without memory. (b) A FRESH PROFILE HAS NO SessionStart HOOK AT ALL, and both hooks in ~/.claude/settings.json hardcode absolute paths into C:/Users/melve/Projects/Self-Improving-Agent. If acquiring one means hand-editing settings.json with an absolute path into one person's home directory, core is installable BY AARON ON THIS MACHINE, which is the proxy the brief forbids.

(2) THE REAL DEFECT: a working-tree copy can disagree with the repository on line endings while git reports clean, and no check sees it. .gitattributes normalises on commit, so git STORES docs/loops/sia-mailbox-decisions.md as LF and `git show HEAD:<path>` returns LF; because `text eol=lf` makes git compare NORMALISED content, a stale CRLF working copy also reads clean in `git status` and in every diff. The repository is correct, one working tree is stale, nothing in the normal workflow reports the difference, and it survives until something forces a re-checkout of that path. A scripted multi-line edit against that file would hit exactly the mismatch the watch-out warns about, ON A FILE GIT SWEARS IS FINE.

## Architecture Overview

3-tier hub-and-spoke memory protocol:

| Tier | Location | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| **Global** | `~/Obsidian Vault/` + `CLAUDE.md` | Cross-project experiences, reusable skills, user preferences |
| **Domain** | Tagged experiences in vault | Stack-specific knowledge (Convex patterns, Stripe gotchas, etc.) |
| **Project** | `.agents/` in each repo | Project-specific context (PRD, tasks, session logs) |

## Search Architecture (v0.6.0)

| Store | Search type | Access |
|---|---|---|
| SQLite FTS5 (knowledge-v2.db) | Keyword + snippet | `kb_recall` via open-brain MCP |
| Obsidian (Summaries/) | Semantic embeddings | `smart-connections__lookup` |
| SQLite vec (knowledge.db) | Semantic vector | Disabled — v1 IDs stale, rebuild pending |

## Key Distinction

- **Self-Improving Agent** = the memory protocol (how knowledge flows across sessions)
- **AI-First Development Framework** = the project template (how projects are structured for AI agents)
- These are complementary layers distributed from this repo, but they are not the same thing
